lessons.context: Wayfarer chapter 1 translation - Thai/Khmer script leak
lessons.lesson: Translation output contained Thai and Khmer characters along with checkbox artifacts (- [○], - []:) and stray markdown headers (## [ in ]). Postprocessor was missing Khmer pattern (U+1780-U+17FF) and Thai wasn't being stripped in the clean pipeline.
lessons.action: Postprocessor must strip ALL non-Myanmar Unicode script blocks: Thai (U+0E00-U+0E7F), Khmer (U+1780-U+17FF), Bengali, Indic, Chinese, Korean. Add checkbox artifact patterns to REASONING_PATTERNS. Stray English headers like ## [ in ] must be detected and stripped.

lessons.context: Wayfarer glossary migration from JSON to SQLite
lessons.lesson: Migrating legacy glossary data requires careful field mapping. The JSON format uses 'source'/'target' while database uses 'source_term'/'target_term'. Verified status in JSON (verified=true or auto_approved=true) maps to database status='approved', otherwise status='pending'. Confidence scores should be higher for verified terms (0.95) vs pending (0.7).
lessons.action: Always create a dedicated migration script with proper field mapping. Check for existing terms before insertion to avoid duplicates. Log migration statistics for verification.

lessons.context: Versioning and Change Tracking System Implementation
lessons.lesson: Building a version control system on top of SQLite requires careful separation of concerns: VersionManager coordinates operations while repositories handle data access. File snapshots must use unique filenames (timestamp with microseconds) to prevent collisions during rapid successive snapshots. Glossary sync jobs need explicit chapter selection (not just auto-detect from usage records) for predictable test behavior.
lessons.action: Always include microseconds in version filenames. Support explicit chapter_nums parameter in sync job creation. Keep VersionManager stateless - all state in database.

lessons.context: Python \b regex corrupts Myanmar compound words
lessons.lesson: Python re module \b treats Myanmar combining marks (Unicode Mn category, e.g. ိ U+102D, ု U+102F) as \W, creating false word boundaries INSIDE syllables. regex \bထို\b matches inside compounds like ထိုင်ခိုင်း → အဲဒီင်ခိုင်း. NEVER use \b for Myanmar text.
lessons.action: Use Myanmar-consonant-specific lookahead/lookbehind: (?<![က-အ])WORD(?!combining*[က-အ]). Also add undo function for pre-existing corruptions.

lessons.context: BOM (U+FEFF) not stripped by Python str.strip()
lessons.lesson: str.strip() only removes whitespace characters. BOM (U+FEFF, Zero Width No-Break Space) is NOT whitespace. Files written with UTF-8-SIG encoding have BOM that breaks heading detection with startswith('#') and regex ^ anchor.
lessons.action: Always .lstrip('\ufeff') or .replace('\ufeff', '') before processing heading lines.

lessons.lesson: padauk-gemma can output Tamil (and potentially other Indic scripts) mixed in Myanmar text. Postprocessor must strip ALL non-Myanmar scripts, not just Chinese/Bengali/Thai.
lessons.action: Added _INDIC_PATTERN covering 9 Indic script blocks. Always strip in clean_output().

lessons.context: Novel: Reverend Insanity — padauk-gemma glossary comparison garbage
lessons.lesson: padauk-gemma at temperature ≥ 0.4 outputs word-by-word glossary comparison junk (*:* "word" is . "other" is .) mixed with translation. These are NOT caught by existing reasoning-stripping patterns. Temperature 0.2 prevents this behavior.
lessons.action: Always use temperature ≤ 0.2 for padauk-gemma. Add *:* pattern detection in postprocessor as defense-in-depth.

lessons.context: Duplicate chapter headings re-appeared after postprocessor fix
lessons.lesson: remove_duplicate_headings() used exact string match but the padauk-gemma model outputs slightly different heading text per chunk (e.g., နှင်းမှုန် vs နှင်းစက်). Prefix matching on '# အခန်း N' pattern is required.
lessons.action: Always use prefix/regex matching for heading deduplication, not exact string comparison.

lessons.lesson: .agent/ directory is the agent brain — must be created before any other operation. All files follow strict schemas defined in AGENTS.md.
lessons.action: Always create .agent/ files with correct schemas on first session

lessons.context: Myanmar paragraph similarity — SequenceMatcher vs char-set overlap
lessons.lesson: Char-set overlap on Myanmar text gives false 80-86% similarity on completely different sentences that share common particles (သည်/ကို/မည်). SequenceMatcher gives true sequence similarity: different sentences score 0.26-0.31, true duplicates score 0.90+.
lessons.action: ALWAYS use SequenceMatcher for Myanmar sentence similarity. NEVER use char-set overlap. Threshold 0.85+ is safe for duplicate detection.

lessons.context: Myanmar sentence ender check — modern prose patterns
lessons.lesson:
Modern Myanmar Wuxia/Xianxia prose regularly uses ! and ? alongside ။. Chapter format may include ---
<subtitle>
--- sectioning where subtitle is not a proper sentence. Both must be excluded from sentence-ender validation.
lessons.action: Add ! and ? to valid_enders. Detect subtitle_lines between --- separators and exclude from content_lines check.

lessons.context: Chapter 003 translation failure — Myanmar ratio 0% after refinement
lessons.lesson: Refiner model (padauk-gemma) can output English instead of Myanmar for certain chunks, causing 0% Myanmar ratio. MYANMAR_PATTERN was missing Extended-B range (U+A9E0-U+A9FF), causing false Thai character detection.
lessons.action: Always include explicit Myanmar language guard in refiner prompts. MYANMAR_PATTERN must include all 3 Myanmar blocks: U+1000-U+109F, U+AA60-U+AA7F, U+A9E0-U+A9FF.

known_patterns.cause: .agent/ directory is not committed to version control (contains session state)
known_patterns.fix: Auto-create .agent/ files from AGENTS.md schema on first run

padauk-gemma:q8_0.notes: Primary EN→MM model. 98%+ Myanmar ratio. Best results with temp=0.2, repeat_penalty=1.15. DO NOT increase temperature above 0.2 — causes glossary comparison garbage (*:* pattern).

alibayram/hunyuan:7b.notes: CN→EN pivot Stage 1 model. Good Chinese comprehension.

qwen:7b.notes: Fast checker model. Produces English not Myanmar — do NOT use as translator. Only suitable for validation tasks.

qwen2.5:14b.notes: Good Chinese comprehension but outputs Japanese/Chinese instead of Myanmar. Use only for CN→EN pivot, not for Myanmar output.
